english: I am well aware of this problem.
tip: известна (izvestna = is known) puts the person who knows in the dative: мне (mne = to me), literally the problem is known to me.

target: Я начинаю день с чашки крепкого кофе.
english: I start my day with a cup of strong coffee.
tip: Here с (s = with) takes the genitive, not the instrumental: с чашки (s chashki = with a cup), meaning starting from.

english: Mathematics comes easily to her.
tip: даётся (dayotsya = comes easily) puts the person in the dative: ей (yey = to her); математика (matematika = maths) stays the subject.

english: He is interested in Russian history.
tip: интересуется (interesuyetsya = is interested) takes the instrumental: русской историей (russkoy istoriyey = in Russian history).

english: The children laugh loudly.
tip: смеются (smeyutsya = they laugh) keeps the -ся ending; the verb смеяться (smeyatsya) has no form without it.

english: I ate soup yesterday.
tip: Past tense agrees with the subject's gender. ела (yela = ate) ends in -ла for a female speaker; a man would say ел (yel).

english: Life is boring without friends.
tip: без (bez = without) takes the genitive: друзей (druzey = of friends) from друзья (druzya).

english: He writes a letter to a friend.
tip: The person you write to goes in the dative: другу (drugu = to a friend) from друг (drug).

english: White seagulls fly over the city.
tip: над (nad = over) takes the instrumental: городом (gorodom = over the city) from город (gorod).

english: He uses a computer every day.
tip: The verb пользуется (polzuetsya = uses) takes the instrumental with no preposition: компьютером (kompyuterom = computer).

english: Instead of sugar, she put salt.
tip: вместо (vmesto = instead of) takes the genitive: сахара (sakhara = of sugar) from сахар (sakhar).

english: Six people are sitting at the table.
tip: After numbers, 'people' uses the count form человек: шесть человек (shest chelavek = six people), not человеков (chelavekov).

english: She draws with a pencil on paper.
tip: The instrumental alone means 'with a tool': карандашом (karandashom = with a pencil), no preposition needed.

english: It seems to me that he is right.
tip: кажется (kazhetsya = it seems) marks the person with the dative: мне (mne = to me) gives 'it seems to me'.

english: I am getting used to the new city.
tip: привыкаю (privykayu = getting used to) takes к plus the dative: к новому городу (k novomu gorodu = to the new city).

target: Он стал чемпионом в прошлом году.
english: He became champion last year.
tip: стал (stal = became) puts the new role in the instrumental: чемпионом (chempionom = champion).

english: Tomorrow the musician will read a book.
tip: Imperfective future is будет (budet = will) plus the infinitive: будет читать (budet chitat = will be reading).

english: She is older than she seems.
tip: старше (starshe = older) is the comparative; add чем (chem = than) to name what you compare with.

target: Мы поехали за город на машине.
english: We drove out to the countryside by car.
tip: за город (za gorod = out of town) uses за plus accusative for motion; за городом (za gorodom) would mean staying there.

target: Разрешите представиться, меня зовут Сергей Николаевич.
english: Allow me to introduce myself, my name is Sergey Nikolaevich.
tip: Russian gives a name with меня зовут (menya zavut = literally 'they call me'), using the accusative меня.

target: Пока он ждал поезд, читал книгу.
english: While he waited for the train, he read a book.
tip: пока (paka = while) pairs with imperfective past for two ongoing actions: ждал (zhdal = was waiting).

english: She turns around.
tip: The reflexive ending -ся (-sya) on оборачивается (abarachivayetsya = turns) points the action back at the subject.

english: Take care of yourself!
tip: For ‘about’ use о (o): позаботься о себе (pazabotsya o sebe = take care of yourself), об (ob) before a vowel.

english: I am afraid of the dark.
tip: The verb боюсь (bayus = I fear) takes its object in the genitive: боюсь темноты (bayus temnaty = afraid of the dark), not the accusative.

english: He will cook dinner.
tip: Imperfective future is будет (budet = will be) plus an unchanged infinitive: будет готовить (budet gatovit = will cook).

english: The singer's voice sounds wonderful.
tip: Possession uses the genitive after the noun: голос певца (golos pevtsa = the singer's voice), literally voice of-the-singer.

english: We were preparing for departure.
tip: готовиться к (gatovitsya k = to prepare for) takes the dative: готовились к отъезду (gatovilis k atyezdu = we prepared for departure).

english: I worry before the exam.
tip: The position word перед (pered = before, in front of) takes the instrumental: перед экзаменом (pered ekzamenom = before the exam).

english: She stops by the window.
tip: у (u = by, near) plus the genitive marks location: у окна (u akna = by the window), from окно (akno = window).

english: I will read this book.
tip: A single perfective verb states the future: прочитаю (prachitayu = I will read and finish), no будет (budet) needed.
